issues.legal_issue: A regularly operating market held by an intermediary, whether in an urban or rural area, and the land and structures comprising it vest in the State upon vesting of the estate.
material_facts: The properties consisted of rows of shops in established commercial centres where buyers and sellers regularly conducted business.
The shops and market sites were held by the intermediaries, who collected rent or fees and maintained the markets.
The markets existed when the estates vested in the State.
issues.conclusion: The market sites and their buildings or structures vested in the State; the Act did not distinguish between urban and rural markets, and collecting tolls was not necessary to constitute a bazar.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 4(a) provide for vesting of the intermediary’s estate and interests in hats, bazars and other specified interests; Sections 5 to 7 preserve only specified interests, while Section 7A prevents the preservation of rights in land on which an intermediary held a hat or bazar in the relevant period before vesting. The Court treated a bazar as a market characterised by regular buying and selling, not merely a periodic rural gathering, and held that the provisions apply without an urban-rural distinction. It relied on State of Bihar v. Rameshwar Pratap Narain Singh, which recognised the right to hold a hat, bazar or mela as an interest in land; Ramesh Bejoy Sharma v. Pasupati Rai on the consequences of vesting; and the vesting principles in State of West Bengal v. Suburban Bar Agriculture & Fisheries, Brighu Nath Sahay Singh v. Md. Khallur Rehman and Smt. Labanya Bala Devi v. State of Bihar. Kanpur Sugar Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar was considered in distinguishing buildings used as markets from buildings used for other specified purposes.

rule.if: land_reform_vesting_proceeding and intermediary_held_market_site and regular_market_activity and market_existed_before_vesting

predicates.land_reform_vesting_proceeding: The dispute concerns whether property in an intermediary’s estate vested in the State under a land-reform vesting scheme.
predicates.intermediary_held_market_site: The intermediary held the land or buildings on which the market was situated, as owner or by virtue of authority or settlement.
predicates.regular_market_activity: Buyers and sellers regularly conducted commercial activity at the site as a continuing feature.
predicates.market_existed_before_vesting: The hat or bazar was held on the site before the estate vested in the State.

issues.definition: When an intermediary held a site where regular market activity existed before vesting, the site and its structures vest in the State in a land-reform vesting proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A commercial market composed of shops is not a homestead saved from vesting merely because a dwelling house previously stood on the site or the shops are let to tenants.
material_facts: The properties at issue consisted of rows of shops used for commercial activity and let to tenants.
At one site, an earlier residential building had been demolished and shops had been constructed before vesting.
The asserted homestead status rested on the previous dwelling use or on the shops being let out.
issues.conclusion: The market properties were not homesteads saved from vesting, and the homestead exception did not apply to them.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(j) defines a homestead by reference to a dwelling house and associated property, and Section 5 saves the intermediary’s interest in qualifying homesteads as a tenancy under the State. Sections 7A and 7B limit the rights that may otherwise be preserved under Sections 5 to 7. The Court held that commercial market shops are not a dwelling house merely because they are let on rent or because a dwelling house previously existed on the land. It considered Kanpur Sugar Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar in distinguishing property used as a specified building from land used for another purpose.

rule.if: land_reform_vesting_proceeding and commercial_market_site and shops_used_for_trade and not site_used_as_dwelling_house

predicates.land_reform_vesting_proceeding: The dispute concerns whether property in an intermediary’s estate vested in the State under a land-reform vesting scheme.
predicates.commercial_market_site: The property is a site functioning as a market rather than as a residential homestead.
predicates.shops_used_for_trade: The buildings on the site are shops used for commercial activity.
predicates.site_used_as_dwelling_house: The site is used as a dwelling house, rather than merely having had a dwelling house on it in the past.

issues.definition: A commercial market site made up of shops used for trade and not used as a dwelling house is not saved as a homestead in a land-reform vesting proceeding.
